transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-01-14 15:00 PST
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Liam (Redwood SE), Rajiv (BrightPath Eng Manager), Priya (BrightPath SRE), Aaron (BrightPath Product), Speaker 4

[00:00] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick agenda — go through the telemetry from yesterdays deploy and then decide reproducer and next steps.
[00:18] Rajiv: Yeah thanks, yeah so we saw an uptick of 5xxs starting ~09:07 UTC, p95 latency stayed okay but p99 spiked and then some requests hit the client-side 60 second timeout.
[00:34] Priya: to add, lots of the 5xx are 502/504 at the edge, somethin — like the gateway returning upstream timeout. we also saw some 429s earlier in the window.
[00:49] Liam: right, two quick clarifications — are the 429s coming before the 5xx surge or coincident? that matters for retry behavior.
[00:56] Rajiv: our timeline shows 429s first as traffic ramps; then we had a retry flood from our app — so believe theres some cascading retries.
[01:12] Maya: ok classic retry storm. can you confirm what your client backoff looked like? linear? no jitter?
[01:18] Aaron: ah yeah, we had a simple 3-retry loop with fixed 1s backoff, no jitter, client side. we thought server-side rate-limiting would keep things in check. clearly not.
[01:30] Liam: that's risky at scale. fixed backoff + multiple concurrent threads is basically synchronized retrying. we recommend exponential backoff + full jitter or at least decorrelated jitter. also consider idempotency tokens for non-idempotent endpoints.
[01:46] Priya: question — could the model update yesterday have increased per-request compute so we were hitting GPU saturations? we saw GPU util climb around the same time.
[01:55] Liam: possible. our telemetry shows CPU/GPU increased by ~8-12% for that model variant at p95 sequence length; there could be longer token decoding paths. we should correlate model token counts with the request trace.
[02:08] Rajiv: we can share a sample trace. There are request IDs from 09:06:57 UTC that line up.
[02:15] Maya: perfect. we'll need those.
[02:18] Speaker 4: (inaudible)
[02:21] Maya: we also noticed higher KV cache miss rate in the logs — Liam, did the config change for prefix caching?
[02:28] Liam: no config change on our side, but the model variant change could change caching locality. if the model expands prompt templates token prefixes mismatch and cache hit drops. that increases per-token work and amplifies latency.
[02:41] Priya: so should we re-enable a stronger cache policy or fall back to a smaller model?
[02:48] Liam: both are options. immediate mitigation: 1) enable a more aggressive prefix/KV caching TTL for the pilot traffic pattern 2) adjust retry/backoff in the client 3) temporarily raise rate-limit thresholds for the pilot consumer in dedicated pool if possible.
[03:05] Rajiv: raising rate-limits sounds like ignoring the root cause — if we increase limits we might just push more load to overloaded GPUs.
[03:13] Maya: agreed, raising limits is a tactical move to reduce upstream 429s while we tune. we should pair that with stricter retries and a circuit breaker.
[03:23] Aaron: can Redwood do per-customer burst capacity? that could help for predictable pilot spikes.
[03:29] Liam: yes, Dedicated or reserved pools can give more predictable throughput but need lead time. there's also short-term burst quotas we can enable.
[03:38] Priya: more urgent — the 60s client timeout. some of our mobile clients give up at 60s and then retry later, so user-visible errors happen. can we reduce server-side tail latency?
[03:48] Liam: we can tune kernel selection and beam decode length caps but that's model-level. also smart batching adjustments — if we lower batch wait thresholds it reduces tail in low-concurrency windows. but at peak, batching helps throughput; tradeoff.
[04:03] Rajiv: thought — what about server-side retry deduplication? if requests are retried due to 429/502, can Redwood dedupe to avoid duplicate GPU work?
[04:12] Liam: we have optional request de-dup based on idempotency keys; it requires client to send a stable request fingerprint. we can enable on a per-route basis in the pilot config.
[04:23] Priya: ok we can add idempotency tokens.
[04:26] Maya: Great. Action plan then: Liam to reproduce under controlled traffic with current client config, then rerun with exponential backoff+jitter and idempotency to demonstrate reduced 5xx. also check KV cache hit rate with the new model.
[04:39] Aaron: one more question on observability — we saw gaps in trace sampling during the incident, some spans missing.
[04:46] Liam: we have an adjustable sampling window; it seems sampling dropped when load spiked because tracing agent started shedding. we can bump sampling for the pilot or export traces asynchronously to avoid shedding.
[05:00] Rajiv: can we get a CSV of p50/p90/p95/p99 before/after for the window?
[05:06] Maya: yes we'll attach that.
[05:08] (longer silence as folks read shared doc)
[05:42] Priya: pragmatic question — what if we temporarily route the pilot through a lower-latency region to reduce network hops? is that easy?
[05:50] Liam: region routing is pretty straightforward, but cold-starts for model variants could shift latencies. we'll estimate cost.
[05:58] Maya: ok to summarize: reproduce, tweak retry/backoff + jitter, add idempotency keys, look at KV cache behavior with new model, optionally adjust rate limits for a short window, and check traces/logs.
[06:12] Rajiv: yep. also please include firewall logs from our side for the 09:07 window.
[06:18] Maya: noted.
[06:21] Aaron: what about long-term — should we plan a canary rollback to the older model if regression persists?
[06:27] Liam: absolutely. our rollout policies support canary and fast rollback; we can coordinate and pin the older variant.
[06:32] Priya: any security/compliance concerns with adding idempotency keys? we need to be sure no PII is in keys.
[06:39] Maya: good call. use hashed tokens or UUIDs not user-identifying fields — we'll put that note in the docs.
[06:46] Rajiv: also curious whether autoscaling was throttled by quota — I saw some 403-ish errors earlier in the logs.
[06:54] Liam: that sounds like a quota enforcement from the cloud provider side or our internal pump — we need the sequences for the 403s to check.
[07:02] Maya: ok, that's in the action items.
[07:05] (discussion moves to timings and owners)
[07:15] Maya: Any blockers to the plan?
[07:18] Priya: none from SRE; we'll get logs.
[07:20] Rajiv: will confirm sample IDs.
[07:22] Aaron: we'll create a small feature flag in our client to toggle improved backoff during the repro window.
[07:28] Maya: perfect. I'll also attach the SOC2 and KMS integration doc you asked about and the pilot extension pricing.
[07:33] Liam: one tiny note — be mindful of cache warming if you change prefixes; a sudden TTL increase can cause cold-start flurries. we'll provide recommended warmup script.
[07:44] Rajiv: nice.
[07:46] Maya: ok let's close with concrete dates: Liam to run repro by Friday 2026-01-16, Priya to provide logs by Thursday 2026-01-15, Maya to send docs by Monday 2026-01-18, and follow up next Wednesday 2026-01-21 for results review.
[07:58] (meeting ends at ~00:55)

Notes: transcription contains a few misheard tokens and a Speaker 4 placeholder; timestamps approximated. Shared artifacts referenced: https://redwood.app/pilots/brightpath/telemetry-20260113.csv and pilot-pricing-v2.pdf
